summary: Ariane Macdonald is a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology who studied under Rolf A. Stein. She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Arindam Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford. He held professorships at the University of Delhi (attested 1999) and the University of Hawaiʻi (attested 2009–2014).
Arinde L. Jonker specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), studying under Jonathan A. Silk and MA supervisor Peter Bisschop.
Aristotle C. Dy is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under doctoral supervisor Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).

Arjo Vanderjagt (born 1948) works in philosophy and history/archaeology. After studying at the University of Groningen (1971–1981), he held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), Utrecht University (2007), and the University of Groningen (1994–2009).

Arlo Griffiths (born 1976) specializes in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard and Leiden (PhD ~1999–2004 under Henk Bodewitz), later holding posts at Leiden (attested 2002–2008), Groningen (~2004–2005), and EFEO (from 2008).

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren (1760–1842) was a historian who studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (PhD 1784). He spent his career at Göttingen, becoming a professor of philosophy in 1794 and history in 1801.

Arnold J. Toynbee (1889–1975) was a historian who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1907–1911). He held positions at King's College London (~1919–1924), Chatham House (~1925–1955), and the London School of Economics (~1925–1955).
Arnold Kirillovich Tulokhonov (born 1949) studied at Irkutsk State University (~1966–1971) and held a post at the Federation Council (~2013–2017).

Arthur Anthony Macdonell (1854–1930) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1888 and held posts at Balliol and Corpus Christi College.

Arthur Berriedale Keith (1879–1944) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, under Julius Eggeling and Arthur Anthony Macdonell, later serving in the Colonial Office (~1901–1914) and as professor at Edinburgh (1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen (1875–1945) was a Danish scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1893–1900) and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding Copenhagen's first chair of Orientalistics (1919–1945).

Arthur Coke Burnell (1840–1882) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College London (~1857–1860) under teachers including Fausbøll, Goldstücker, and Jäschke. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1860–1880).
Arthur Evans (1851–1941) was a historian and archaeologist. He was educated at Harrow School (~1866–1870) and Brasenose College, Oxford (1870), and taught John Marshall.

Arthur F. Wright (1913–1976) was a scholar of Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard (under John King Fairbank), and held professorships at Stanford (1958) and Yale (1959, 1961).

Arthur Llewellyn Basham (1914–1986) was an Indologist and historian who studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He held posts at SOAS (1948–1965) and later served as professor at the Australian National University (~1965–1978).
Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard University (attested 2005) under Diana L. Eck, Parimal G. Patil, and Palri Sangye.

Arthur Schopenhauer (1788–1860) was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Jena (PhD 1813). His teachers included Majer, Schleiermacher, Boeckh, and Wolf. He held a lecturing post at the University of Berlin (~1820–1831).

Arthur Venis (1857–1918) was an Indologist educated at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as professor and principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1881–1888) and taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (~1888–1914).

Arthur Waley (1889–1966) was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at King's College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1913–1929) and held an honorary lectureship at SOAS in 1948.
